source: MAFF/JICA APPP (Agricultural Productivity Promotion Project in West Tonle Sap) Farmer Field School Technical Manual for Extension Officers, December 2014 -- no elibrary URL visible on this scan.
province: Battambang, Pursat, Kampong Chhnang (APPP project area)
text: Farmers using traditional transplanting (ការស្ទូង) benefit from planting seedlings in straight, evenly spaced rows rather than clumping many seedlings together at random. The recommended spacing is about 20 cm between hills within a row and about 25 cm between rows (20 x 25 cm), using seedlings around 21 days old. Plant only 2-3 seedlings per hill (គុម្ព), rather than the older habit of packing 5-10 seedlings into each hill. Even spacing between hills allows better airflow and sunlight around each plant, supporting more even tillering and growth, and makes it easier to walk between rows for weeding and crop checks. Apply a basal DAP fertilizer application of roughly 40-50 kg per hectare at transplanting time or shortly before. A simple way to lay out straight rows without special equipment is to stretch a length of rope marked at regular intervals (for example, tied with colored string every 20 cm) between two people at opposite edges of the field, and use it as a sighting line so each row of seedlings stays straight both along the row and across it.
